# sing-box-vps documentation index

Project: https://github.com/KnowSky404/sing-box-vps
Wiki: https://github.com/KnowSky404/sing-box-vps/wiki
Runtime authority: install.sh; sbv commands --json for the versioned operation catalog, sbv schema <operation-id> --json for argument/safety/input contracts, and sbv agent capabilities --json for compatible product capabilities.
Installer authoring: src/install/manifest.txt and source fragments; generate install.sh with bash scripts/build-install.sh, then check with --check.
Core baseline: sing-box 1.14.4. Use route/outbound direct rules; action:direct is removed. Linux ARM64 1.14.2 and 1.14.4 with_purego namespace use is refused. See docs/wiki/Protocol-Coverage.md and Advanced-Components.md for build/evidence boundaries.

Read AGENTS.md and skills/sing-box-vps-operator/SKILL.md before repository or VPS operations.
Security reviewers: read SECURITY.md for the threat model, review priorities and finding format. Read-only review does not trigger implementation or broad testing. Local current-HEAD/full-diff review is required before push/PR. Remote reviews are automatic only: never manually trigger Code Review or Security Review. Wait only for automatically triggered current-head Security Review; if none triggered, record not_triggered and merge after local review, validation and required GitHub checks pass. Unreadable/running/failed review state is not absence; handle reported findings.
Use sing-box-test for test hosts; production is sing-box-prod. Unknown hosts are production until clarified. Production mutations require an approved operation plan.

Documentation sources (also available offline):
- docs/wiki/Home.md: navigation.
- docs/wiki/Management.md: server network menu, draft application/recovery and node-sharing scope.
- docs/wiki/Storage-Layout.md: unified private root, legacy storage status/migrate/recover and service/backup boundaries.
- docs/wiki/Getting-Started.md: staged installation/uninstallation and country-city REALITY candidates with development checker evidence; always recheck from the installing VPS.
- docs/wiki/Command-Catalog.md: generated operation reference, exact usage, safety boundaries and explicit interactive-only limitations.
- docs/wiki/Agent-CLI.md: commands, confirmation, revision/CAS and sensitive output.
- docs/wiki/Agent-Runbook.md: operations, upgrade, troubleshooting and recovery.
- docs/wiki/Protocol-Instances.md: typed protocol contracts.
- docs/wiki/Advanced-Components.md: component ownership and lifecycle.
- docs/wiki/Protocol-Coverage.md: implementation and evidence boundaries.
- docs/wiki/HY2-ACME.md: automatic certificates and focused verification.
- docs/wiki/Upgrade-Rehearsal.md: fixed-version upgrade rehearsal.
- docs/wiki/Development.md: contribution, atomic --test selection with full --base diff checks, runtime scope, REALITY candidate public-checker/evidence gate and Wiki publication.
- docs/specs/README.md: implementation contracts, completion evidence and outstanding acceptance boundaries.
- docs/specs/scoped-docker-verification.md: complete outbound/policy decomposition, 13 protocol_probe_* leaves, Naive/Snell transitions and protocol_coexistence; fresh SOCKS/CAS/owned-fixture prerequisites, explicit REALITY/Tor external boundaries, original 17-scenario full compatibility, Stage 1 history and the accepted 32 independent real-Docker scenes plus aggregate compatibility (33/33), with timing boundaries distinguishing internal installations from separately scheduled baselines (Chinese counterpart: docs/specs/scoped-docker-verification.zh-CN.md).

Each added/changed runtime operation must update its noninteractive command, embedded descriptor, focused tests, generated command reference and affected runbooks/Agent navigation. Build install.sh, generate the reference with scripts/build-command-docs.sh, and check both with --check plus tests/command_catalog_contract.sh. Do not automate prompt answers. Routing export input is the private raw .data.draft object, not the response envelope; preserve fingerprint CAS. Service logs and full routing drafts are sensitive.

Never print credentials or full links in shared logs. Config changes require sing-box check. Local/mock, Docker, public, external-provider and production evidence are independent.

Storage preflight: read storage status blockers and blocker_details (entry/path/reason); ok=true only confirms a successful read. Verify source integrity before repairing a historical owner; preserve unmanaged libraries.

Legacy backup archives: private root-owned directories may contain historical foreign-UID regular files; never execute archive contents. Live runtime and recovery control files remain root-owned. Diagnose untrusted_legacy_backups via blocker_details; cleanup needs separate authorization and completed migration verification.

Lifecycle debt contract: docs/specs/technical-debt-remediation.md (Chinese: docs/specs/technical-debt-remediation.zh-CN.md). Menu service controls share Agent guards; uninstall must confirm stopped state and reclaim ledger-owned firewall rules before deleting runtime. Interrupted SubMan writes need readback reconciliation. CI scope is baseline-bound and host-only, never Docker/production proof.

Protocol defaults and HY2 preflight: docs/wiki/Protocol-Instances.md#tcp-fast-open-and-hy2-defaults; sbv hy2 masquerade-check --json [--url URL] lists REALITY website candidates and checks HTTP(S), never reuses the HY2 TLS identity. New supported TCP listeners default TFO on; AnyTLS outbound is excluded. HY2 menu creation defaults Salamander on; explicit JSON obfs values remain authoritative.

GitHub Actions authorization: AGENTS.md section 4.2.1 and docs/wiki/Development.md. No CI dispatch/rerun or indirect Actions trigger without explicit user authorization for the workflow/ref/scope. Push/PR/merge authorization does not include CI. Workflows are manual-only; unauthorized CI is not_run_not_authorized, never passed.
WARP media safety: docs/specs/warp-media-session-safety.md; menu 12 -> 4 reuses an existing authenticated SOCKS/HTTP/Mixed ingress pinned to warp-ep, verifies WARP trace, and refuses ambiguous routes. Never launch a second endpoint with production WARP identity. Other ingress protocols require a separately approved solution; diagnostics never add listeners or change routing.
